Ugmuls 5.5e Automation · Detailed Summary

Class features.
Built into the roll.

Class abilities connected to your native attacks, damage rolls, saves, and chat cards.

Automations → Unique Classes

Your class abilities,
right when you need them.

Choose your smite, unleash a maneuver, or add your class’s extra damage as you make the attack. Relevant options appear in the roll, with a preview of the damage you’re about to deal. The module tracks supported resources and once-per-turn uses, helping players focus on their next move and giving the GM less to keep track of. Explore the class sections below to see what’s supported.

Artificer

Supported official Eberron features join the native roll workflow. Enable the corresponding options for your table.

  • Flash of Genius Click the button on a failed check/save to add Intelligence (minimum +1) to the original result. A native feature use is spent even if it still fails; combat also tracks the Reaction. Eligible self/visible recipients must be within 30 feet. Unknown-DC rolls require failure confirmation.
  • Arcane Jolt · destructive energy Select the optional rider on confirmed-hit damage. The Artificer needs a magic weapon; a natively linked Steel Defender draws from the Artificer’s feature uses. Both share the once-per-combat-turn limit. Damage follows native scaling and critical rules. Canceled previews spend nothing; healing remains manual.
  • Arcane Firearm Confirm the firearm in eligible Artificer spell damage configuration to add one typed 1d8 per cast. Mixed damage offers a type choice. The separate bonus does not double on a critical and spends no charges. Weapons, cannons and other classes’ spells are excluded.

Steel Defender reaction timing remains manual.

Barbarian

CoreBerserkerWild HeartWorld Tree

Barbarians live to attack. With so many features triggered by an attack or damage roll, going back to add dice or adjust results can get confusing. Now those choices are built right into your Attack and Damage rolls—choose your strike, add your damage, and keep the fight moving.

  • Reckless Attack On your first attack, use Reckless above Advantage to apply the native effect and roll. Strength attacks gain advantage until your next turn; attacks against you also gain advantage. Disadvantage combines normally.
  • Frenzy While Rage and Reckless are active, the first qualifying Strength-based weapon hit on your turn includes the configured damage rider, with critical support.
  • Zealot · Divine Fury While raging, your first weapon or Unarmed Strike hit on your turn adds 1d6 plus half your Barbarian level. Choose Radiant or Necrotic in damage Configuration; the dice roll with the initial damage and support critical hits.
  • Zealot · Fanatical Focus A failed-save card offers one replacement d20 plus your Rage Damage bonus, once per active Rage. Previous advantage/disadvantage is not reused; the new result is mandatory. Recorded targeting is restored after the reroll.
  • Zealot · Zealous Presence Recipients gain advantage on attacks and saves until the start of the source Barbarian’s next turn. Attacking does not consume it; other sources and AC5E combine normally.
  • Brutal Strike Use Brutal above Normal for a Strength attack on your turn without disadvantage. It activates Reckless on your first attack or reuses active Reckless later, forgoes advantage, and uses your one chosen Brutal attack for the turn even on a miss.
  • Brutal effects in damage Configuration Hits include scaled Brutal damage with the weapon roll. Choose Forceful or Hamstring Blow; Improved Brutal Strike adds Staggering and Sundering, and Improved Brutal Strike (2) allows two different effects. Native Hamstrung, Staggered, and Sundered effects apply to hit targets, expire at your next turn start, and support Apply/Undo. Movement stays manual.
  • Sundered The next single-target attack by someone other than the source Barbarian gains +5, once, then consumes eligible Sundered effects whether it hits or misses. Canceling the prompt preserves the effect.
  • Staggered The next saving throw has disadvantage through AC5E or the standalone flow. Magic Resistance advantage cancels it to Normal. After that save, the native effect stays until expiry for its Opportunity Attack restriction.

Rage, Strength and staying on your feet

  • Indomitable Might. Qualifying Strength checks and saves use the Strength score when the rolled total is lower. The roll retains its dice and modifiers, and the replaced total is labeled. Skills and tools qualify only when actually rolled with Strength.
  • Linked Rage benefits. Primal Knowledge is applied and removed with Rage. Rage ends when the supported incapacitating/Unconscious flow requires it. Relentless Rage offers the native Constitution save at 0 HP and applies its successful healing through the existing workflow, retaining the feature’s increasing DC tracker.
  • Reckless cleanup. Repeated activations reuse expired or disabled Reckless Attack effects rather than leaving a new copy each turn.

Berserker

  • Mindless Rage. The linked benefit follows Rage, supplies native Charmed/Frightened immunity and ends those conditions when Rage starts. It is removed when Rage ends.
  • Intimidating Presence. The area excludes the Barbarian. Its supported Frightened effect receives repeat saves and normal effect application/cleanup. Frenzy remains integrated into qualifying damage rolls.

Wild Heart

  • Choose before Rage. Rage of the Wilds offers Eagle, Bear or Wolf. With Power of the Wilds, a second column requires Falcon, Lion or Ram before Rage is activated or resources are spent. Canceling spends nothing.
  • Benefits follow the choice. Bear uses native resistance; Wolf supplies a linked aura for contextual ally attack Advantage. Lion has its own linked aura for supported enemy Disadvantage, keeping it independent of Wolf. Falcon adds flight; armor eligibility stays manual. Eagle’s Dash/Disengage remains manual.
  • Ram and Aspects. After a qualifying hit, the optional Ram button applies native Prone directly through the GM. Aspect of the Wilds posts an owner/GM choice card for Owl, Panther or Salmon, replacing the prior aspect. Daily switching restrictions remain manual.

World Tree

  • Vitality Surge. Activating Rage automatically grants temporary HP equal to Barbarian level without a second card or click, preserving a higher existing amount. Extending Rage does not refill it.
  • Life-Giving Force. Activate the native activity manually for its healing roll. The module clears the Pending label once the roll completes; the other World Tree choices and temporary-HP ending decisions remain manual.

Bard

Bards live to inspire. They live to taunt. Adding your dice to an existing roll no longer means working it out afterward. Prompts appear directly on eligible rolls, only when you have the resources to spend, and automatically use the right die size.

  • Bardic Inspiration Inspire automatically applies the configured Inspired effect and records the source Bard’s die. A failed attack, save, or ability check can add that die without rerolling the original d20. Rolling spends the grant; unknown-DC tests request confirmation or a DC.
  • Lore · Cutting Words Eligible enemy attack-hit and damage cards offer Cutting Words within 60 feet, with a Reaction and Inspiration use available. Original dice remain; damage components are selectable and cannot fall below zero. Sight walls block eligibility and users confirm visibility. Undo applied damage before adjusting it.
  • Lore · Peerless Skill Add your current Inspiration die to your own failed attack or ability check. The original roll stays; the resource is spent only when the adjusted test succeeds.
  • Valor · Combat Inspiration damage A default-No damage Configuration choice adds the granted Inspiration die to the initial attack damage, including criticals. Confirming spends Inspired; canceling preserves it.
  • Valor · Combat Inspiration defense An incoming hit offers the recipient a Reaction to add the granted die to AC against that attack. It combines with Shield and consumes the existing Inspired grant rather than another use from the Bard.

Fighter

CorePsi WarriorChampionArcane ArcherBanneret

Battle Masters live for the fight. Choose maneuvers at the point of use in damage Configuration, with attack and damage card actions where needed. No awkward updates or manual dice rerolls—pick your maneuver, take the shot, and keep the fight moving.

Learned maneuvers use Combat Superiority’s available charges and the character’s current die, including d10 and d12 progression. One maneuver can be used per attack. Damage riders join the weapon’s roll and support critical hits.

  • Precision Attack A missed attack card offers Precision Attack. Add the Superiority Die to the original attack without rerolling its d20. Undo applied damage before correcting an attack.
  • Trip Attack Adds damage and prompts a Strength save for Large or smaller targets. Failure toggles the native Prone condition, compatible with standard condition controls and Automated Conditions 5e.
  • Distracting Strike Adds damage and grants advantage to the next attack by a creature other than the Fighter. The effect clears after that attack or at the start of the Fighter’s next turn.
  • Menacing Attack Adds damage and prompts a Wisdom save. Failure applies native Frightened, linked to the Fighter until the end of their next turn.
  • Goading Attack Adds damage and prompts a Wisdom save. Failure causes disadvantage on attacks against creatures other than the Fighter until the end of the Fighter’s next turn. Existing advantage cancels that disadvantage normally.
  • Maneuvering Attack Adds the current Superiority Die to damage and a reminder tag. Choosing the ally, spending their reaction, and moving remain manual.
  • Pushing Attack Adds damage and prompts a Strength save for Large or smaller targets. The card reminds the GM to resolve a failed save’s push of up to 15 feet directly away; movement remains manual.
  • Relentless Characters with the feature gain a Superiority Die dropdown beneath Maneuver. Spend the current die by default, or select d8 — Free (Relentless). The free use is shared across maneuvers, including Precision Attack, once per active combat turn. It becomes available on the next creature’s turn, allowing a qualifying reaction maneuver. With no normal dice left, the free d8 is selected when available. Canceling does not spend it.
  • Cards, effects, and settings Reminder tags identify Goading, Maneuvering, Pushing, and Relentless. Applicable effects retain Apply/Undo controls. Find individual maneuver and Relentless settings under Automations → Unique Classes → Fighter.
  • Parry Incoming single-target melee damage cards offer Parry when a Reaction and Superiority Die are available. It reduces the existing damage, spends the die, and marks the Reaction used. Undo already-applied damage first.

Great Weapon Fighting and Great Weapon Master are under Feats. Other maneuvers remain manual.

Core Fighter

  • Indomitable. A failed-save card offers the native feature use. Reroll one d20, add the Fighter-level bonus and keep the replacement result. The DC and other bonuses stay connected. Undo applied damage or effects before changing a resolved outcome.
  • Studied Attacks. A miss records that creature for Advantage on the next attack against it. Canceling or attacking another creature preserves the benefit; a committed attack consumes it. The marker expires at the end of the Fighter’s next turn. Vex and normal Advantage/Disadvantage cancellation remain separate.

Psi Warrior

  • Psionic Strike. After qualifying weapon damage is applied, use the damage-card action to spend one Fighter Psionic Energy Die and roll the extra Force damage. It is limited to once on the Fighter’s own turn and checks the feature’s range. Damage is normally noncritical; its class setting can make it follow the original attack’s critical result.
  • Telekinetic Thrust. With Telekinetic Adept, the Psionic Strike popup offers Damage Only, Prone or Push. The selected native Strength save begins alongside the Force damage roll. Failure can apply Prone; movement for Push remains manual. No second Energy Die is charged.
  • Protective Field. An incoming damage card offers the Reaction for self or a friendly creature within range. Spend an Energy Die to reduce that recipient’s damage before application. The card total and expanded breakdown show the reduction, other recipients retain their original damage, and Dice So Nice presentation completes before the result is revealed.
  • Native and manual benefits. Bulwark of Force retains native effect use. The module avoids duplicated cover AC with AC5e/Simple Cover; calculating cover remains those integrations’ job. Guarded Mind and ending Bulwark when the Fighter goes down remain table-managed.

Champion

  • Survivor · Heroic Rally. At turn start, a Bloodied Fighter with at least 1 HP gets the native healing card for 5 + Constitution modifier. The owner receives the automated healing Roll prompt unless it is bypassed in Common settings. Disable the native Survivor passive effect to pause. Heroic Warrior and death saves stay manual.

Arcane Archer

  • Activate shots manually. Use the native shot card after the qualifying attack. The module does not choose a shot, automate Curving Shot or add shot damage to weapon configuration.
  • Effects finish on time. Banishing, Shadow and Enfeebling effects expire at the end of the target’s next turn. Enfeebling uses the originating Fighter’s die; expanded damage breakdowns display its reduction.
  • Grasping Shot. A turn-start action prompt offers the recorded Athletics escape check without forcing a roll. Reusing the shot clears the same archer’s prior brambles. Movement and its related table decisions remain manual.

Banneret

  • Group Recovery and Team Tactics. Activate the native cards manually, then choose allies from the map-synced list. Self is excluded and the selector enforces the Charisma-based limit and activity range. Team Tactics applies Advantage on D20 Tests through the start of the Banneret’s next turn. Targeting Regions clear at turn end.
  • Shared Resilience. A qualifying failed ally save offers the Reaction. Spend the native Indomitable use, reroll with the Fighter-level bonus and keep the new result. Available to the owner and GM, with resource tracking and the usual requirement to Undo already-applied outcomes first.
  • Other Fighter features. Tactical Mind, situational movement and Eldritch Knight interactions stay on the native cards or at the table.

Monk

Core & FlurryOpen HandMercyElementsMystic Arts

Strike hard. Strike fast. Masters of unarmed combat, Monks move quickly and attack just as fast. Choose Stunning Strike and Grapple right in damage Configuration, keeping those decisions together at the actual damage roll so you can keep the fight moving.

  • Stunning Strike On a qualifying Monk-weapon or Unarmed Strike hit, damage Configuration offers a default-No choice. Confirming Yes spends 1 Focus Point and prompts the native Constitution save, once per combat turn.
  • Failed and successful saves Failure applies Stunned. Success halves Speed and grants advantage on the next attack against the creature. These effects last until the start of the Monk’s next turn.
  • Stun before Grapple When combined with Grapple, Stunning Strike resolves first, including its animation and automatic effects. A Stunned target automatically fails the following Strength/Dexterity save.
  • Independent corrections Undo Effect restores the Apply control and unlocks Stunning Strike’s rolled save adjustments independently of weapon damage. Reapplication locks its save again.

Shared Grapple / Prone prompts are under Common; Grappler’s feat benefits have their own Feats setting.

Deflection, rerolls and Flurry

  • Deflect Attacks / Deflect Energy. Incoming attack damage cards offer a Reaction reduction using the native formula, without using the source item’s healing activity. Base Deflect requires Bludgeoning, Piercing or Slashing attack damage; Energy extends it to other attack damage types. If reduced to zero, spend Focus to redirect with target/range checks, the native save and Martial Arts damage. Use before HP application.
  • Disciplined Survivor. Use the save-card action to spend Focus for the replacement roll. After it is used, Advantage/Normal/Disadvantage adjustment controls lock so only the replacement result is used.
  • Flurry of Blows. Using Flurry from Monk’s Focus or Heightened Focus opens a remaining-attacks counter: two normally, three with Heightened Focus. Each attack lets you choose a target, uses Empowered Strikes when present and otherwise Unarmed Strike, and counts down after completion. The Grappler feat’s attack-action benefit is excluded; normal damage-replacing Grapple remains possible.

Open Hand

  • Flurry techniques. Attacks launched from the Flurry counter offer the owned Open Hand techniques in damage configuration. Supported saves and effects follow the hit; forced movement remains manual. Other Open Hand activities remain on their native cards.

Mercy

  • Hand of Harm. A qualifying Unarmed/Empowered Strike damage card offers Harm after actual damage. Spend one Focus Point, once per turn. Harm defaults to normal damage; an optional class setting lets it follow a critical. Physician’s Touch adds its Poisoned rider when owned, with source-next-turn-end expiry.
  • Hand of Healing. The Flurry counter can replace one remaining attack with a touch-range healing action, with no additional Focus cost. Normal Flurry permits one healing replacement; failed or canceled rolls retain the attack.
  • Flurry of Healing and Harm. Enable the button before the first completed Flurry attack. It spends one native daily use, announces activation, unlocks further healing replacements and offers free Harm on that Flurry’s attacks. Paid and free Harm share the once-per-turn limit. After the first attack, an unused activation option disappears.

Elements

  • Elemental Push / Pull. Elemental Strike damage configuration offers a default-None direction choice beneath Grapple. The native Strength save names the chosen direction; no extra Focus is charged. It can be combined with Grapple and Stunning Strike while preserving their explicit save order. Movement stays manual.
  • Elemental Epitome. During Attunement, select one resistance from its native card; another choice replaces the old one. Activating Attunement opens the selector, and ending it removes the managed resistance.
  • Destructive Stride. Step of the Wind adds the supported speed benefit and a linked aura through the end of the turn. Enemies encountered join one damage-only card, once per creature, with no save. Players can see recorded targets and the owner/GM can Retarget the card.
  • Empowered Strikes. A default-No damage option adds the native Martial Arts die in the strike’s damage type, once on the Monk’s own turn.

Mystic Arts and manual choices

  • Focused Strike. After Stunning Strike resolves, success or failure applies source-specific Disadvantage against that Monk’s spells until their next turn starts. AC5e handles contextual recommendations with a native fallback.
  • Leave movement and casting flexible. Casting during Flurry, Shadow movement and other situational choices remain manual. The player can close the attack counter and use the native spell or feature.

Paladin

Holy warriors. Masters of the smite. Focus on landing that critical hit, not juggling extra buttons. Divine Smite and supported prepared Smite spells are built into damage Configuration, so you can choose your smite where the damage happens and bring divine judgment down on your enemies.

  • Divine Smite Eligible melee weapon hit damage offers the feature’s available free cast or a spell-slot selection. The chosen resource and bonus action are consumed; slot-funded casts also use the character spell-slot tracker.
  • Fiend and Undead bonus A golden glow and underline indicate that the target qualifies for an extra d8. The info icon explains the bonus. Damage scales with the selected slot and follows the attack’s critical damage.
  • Prepared Smite spells Choose a supported prepared 2024 Smite spell in damage Configuration instead of Divine Smite. A separate Smite Level row stays blank and disabled until a spell is selected, then defaults to a free use or the lowest qualifying slot, with upcasting available. Its initial damage joins the weapon’s roll and follows the critical result. The selected slot/free use and bonus action are spent once.
  • Saves and effects Only Smites requiring a save create a separate save card. Their effects apply on failure, or directly when no save is needed, under the existing application settings. A Smite tag on the damage card shows your choice. Lingering damage and saves use the creature-trigger library.

One unified Paladin aura

One token-attached Region combines Protection, Courage and supported Devotion, Ancients, Glory and Genie benefits. Range follows native preparation or level-based 10/30-foot scaling. Protection uses the source’s Charisma (minimum +1), with the strongest bonus or chosen provider rather than stacking. Incapacitating conditions pause benefits; received effects name the granting Paladin.

Use the actor-window Paladin aura controls to enable a source or choose a preferred Protection provider. Genie Elemental Shielding uses its native feature card: select one resistance, and a later choice replaces the previous one and updates the aura. This choice stays manual, even with automatic effect application enabled.

Disable old Aura Effects Paladin emitters first. Aura outlines show only on the Regions layer. Use Grid Shaped emanations with scene grid spacing and distance matched to the map. Tested with alternating 1–2–1 diagonals; other diagonal rules are unverified.

Supported oath features

  • Noble Genies · Elemental Smite Choose on the completed Divine Smite damage card, including Smites selected with a weapon attack. Spend one Channel Divinity use per cast. Dao applies linked Grappled/Restrained with optional action escape checks; Djinni grants native defenses through the end of your next turn. Efreeti offers an enemy-only second target within 30 feet, synchronized with map targeting, then Normal/Critical damage with the original hit’s critical recommended. With no second enemy it rolls against the original target. Marid offers additional targets for native Strength saves; neither picker includes the caster. Teleports and forced movement remain manual.
  • Noble Genies · Elemental Rebuke Use the reaction button on a confirmed incoming hit/unapplied damage card. Choose an element in the dropdown; native uses and combat Reaction are consumed. Only the Paladin’s damage selector becomes ½, with manual overrides and Undo preserved. The attacker’s Dexterity save and return damage follow; the clicking owner/GM receives the damage prompt. Undo already applied incoming damage before reacting.
  • Ancients · Nature’s Wrath The native initial save and Restrained effect remain. At the victim’s turn end, prompt a Strength save at the recorded Paladin DC; success removes that originating effect. No extra action restrictions or recurring Channel Divinity costs.
  • Devotion · Sacred Weapon Activate from equipped melee attack configuration. Spend Channel Divinity, apply the native enchantment and reopen the attack with its bonus. A temporary actor effect controls the enhancement and 20-foot bright/40-foot dim light. Disable, delete, expiry or unequipping removes benefits and restores prior lighting. Reenable within the remaining duration without another use.
  • Devotion · Smite of Protection Divine Smite activates native half-cover status for you and allies through the existing aura until your next turn starts. Simple Cover 5e and AC5e handle cover calculations, stronger cover and bypasses such as Sharpshooter. No separate cover geometry or flat bonus is calculated here.
  • Devotion · Holy Nimbus Use the native feature to activate temporary Nimbus benefits: enemy turn-start Radiant damage (Charisma + proficiency), Holy Ward save Advantage against Fiend/Undead sources, and aura-radius bright illumination. The controller stops new benefits on disable/expiry. Lighting coordinates with Sacred Weapon. Specialized sunlight interactions may require manual handling.
  • Vengeance · Vow of Enmity Activate in weapon/unarmed attack configuration against a visible creature within 30 feet. The one-minute mark grants target-specific Advantage, with normal Disadvantage cancellation. Transfer free after its target reaches 0 HP without resetting duration, or spend another use for a new Vow. Missing/deleted targets are not assumed dead. Activations and transfers announce themselves before the attack resumes.
  • Vengeance · Avenging Angel Native activation retains ten-minute flight/hover and resource handling. Enemies starting turns in the aura make Wisdom saves; failure applies source-tagged Frightened for one minute or until damage, granting supported attacks Advantage against that frightened target. Success grants no future immunity and does not remove earlier ongoing fear. Leaving the aura does not end the target’s existing fear.

Elder Champion, Noble Scion/Minor Wish, Soul of Vengeance, Relentless Avenger, Inspiring Smite allocation and Living Legend remain table-managed. Keep an active GM connected for managed operations.

Ranger

CoreHunterBeast MasterGloom StalkerFey WandererHollow WardenWinter Walker

Stalk your prey. Know your prey. Hunt your prey. Let the system help track your bonus damage, with Hunter’s Mark and Hunter’s Prey built into damage Configuration. Keep your focus on the hunt while eligible riders join the attack’s damage roll.

  • Hunter’s Prey / Colossus Slayer With Colossus Slayer selected in Hunter’s Prey, adds the configured extra damage against an injured single target, once per combat turn. The selector initially defaults to No and remembers the previous choice. Full-health targets disable it; damage matches the weapon and supports criticals.

Hunter’s Mark is grouped with Spells because its rider follows the caster’s concentration and marked target.

Hunter’s Mark and core Ranger features

  • Relentless Hunter. Damage-triggered concentration checks for the Ranger’s Hunter’s Mark automatically pass without a roll. Other spells and other reasons concentration ends remain unchanged.
  • Precise Hunter and Foe Slayer. Recommend Advantage against the source Ranger’s marked target, combining normally with Disadvantage. Foe Slayer upgrades the integrated Hunter’s Mark rider from d6 to d10 while preserving critical support.

Hunter

  • Choose during a rest. Short and Long Rest dialogs include Ranger Options for Hunter’s Prey and Defensive Tactics, with current choices preselected. Apply changes only after completing the rest. Colossus Slayer enables its damage option; Horde Breaker stays a manual extra attack.
  • Defensive Tactics. Escape the Horde uses this table interpretation: an attack against the Ranger during the Ranger’s own turn is an opportunity attack and recommends Disadvantage. Multiattack Defense tracks the triggering attacker and recommends Disadvantage on its subsequent attacks for the current turn.
  • Superior Hunter’s Defense. An incoming damage-card Reaction lets the owner/GM choose a resistance type. The popup shows the current damage breakdown and preselects the largest type. Apply the resistance to that hit and through the current turn, without changing shared dice or unrelated damage types.
  • Superior Hunter’s Prey. After applied damage to the current mark, choose another enemy within 30 feet of that target using the map-synced picker. Reuse the already-rolled Hunter’s Mark damage, including critical/Foe Slayer results, rather than rolling it again. The second target’s resistances apply normally; once-per-turn tracking and Undo remain available.

Beast Master

  • Bestial Fury. A natively linked Primal Companion gains the supported Force damage against its owning Ranger’s active Hunter’s Mark target, using the Ranger’s Mark die and independent turn tracking. Companion commands, its two attacks and Share Spells remain manual.

Gloom Stalker

  • Dreadful Strike. Damage configuration offers the native extra Psychic damage, spends its use and tracks its turn limit. Ambusher’s Leap applies its first-turn speed benefit and refreshes Argon’s movement display without resetting movement already spent.
  • Stalker’s Flurry. With Dreadful Strike selected, Mass Fear defaults to No. Yes starts the native area Wisdom save alongside damage, with Frightened ending at the Ranger’s next turn start. No offers Sudden Strike on the completed damage card. Shadowy Dodge remains manual with the existing roll-mode controls.

Fey Wanderer

  • Dreadful Strikes. Damage configuration defaults to Yes for 1d4 Psychic, increasing to 1d6 at Ranger level 11. Each creature can receive it once per turn from that Ranger, so striking two different creatures can add it to both.
  • Beguiling Twist. Activate manually, then choose Charmed or Frightened on the save card. Apply only the chosen condition on failure. End-turn Wisdom repeat saves use the recorded DC and clear it on success without another Reaction or resource charge.
  • Misty Wanderer. Owning it adds a managed native cast activity to Misty Step. It spends one feature use with no spell slot and retains normal casting hooks. Regular casting remains available. Companion teleport placement and Fey Reinforcements stay manual.

Hollow Warden

  • Wrath of the Wild. Keep native transformation and armor benefits. The applied form gains a linked, grid-shaped 10-foot enemy-only Unnerving Aura, visible on the Regions layer. Prompt Wisdom saves on adoption and Ranger turn start; failed-save Frightened ends at the Ranger’s next turn start, even after leaving the area. Movement/entry does not trigger saves.
  • Hungering Might. A confirmed attack hit while transformed and Bloodied offers the native 1d10 + Wisdom healing, once per turn. Eligibility uses actual HP rather than requiring a Bloodied icon. The owner receives a Roll prompt by default; normal healing application settings still apply.
  • Rot and Violence. The failed-save aura effect also prevents HP recovery and Reactions through the Ranger’s next turn. Strangling Roots adds a Sap/Slow choice in attack configuration alongside a different base weapon mastery. It starts on Sap and remembers the user’s last used choice.
  • Ancient Might. While transformed, attacks against Frightened targets automatically include the extra Wisdom modifier as Ominous Strikes. This flat bonus does not double on criticals. Persistent Wrath and other deferred situational features remain manual.

Winter Walker

  • Frigid Explorer. Polar Strikes appears in weapon damage configuration, default Yes: 1d4 Cold, increasing to 1d6 at Ranger level 11, once per target per turn. The managed Biting Cold passive effect bypasses Cold resistance for weapon attacks and Ranger spells/features, preserving immunity. Disable that effect to suspend the bypass.
  • Hunter’s Rime. A fresh Hunter’s Mark cast, including a free cast, creates the native 1d10 + Ranger level temporary-HP roll for the Ranger only. Moving the mark does not grant it again. Disengage restrictions remain manual.
  • Fortifying Soul. Use its native healing and one-hour effect. While the effect is active, identified saves that apply Frightened or repeat saves to end it gain Advantage. Saves without a recorded fear source remain manual.
  • Chilling Retribution. The attacker’s damage card offers the Ranger/GM a Reaction, including after damage is applied. Spend one feature use and prompt the attacker’s Wisdom save. Failure applies Stunned and Speed 0 until the end of the Ranger’s next turn. The triggering hit’s damage is unchanged.
  • Frozen Haunt. Activate the native form manually when casting Hunter’s Mark. The linked 15-foot, grid-shaped aura prompts 2d4 Cold damage against enemies on adoption and Ranger turn start, with no entry/movement damage. It follows the token and clears when the form ends. Native immunities, moving through objects and shunting stay as configured or manual.

Rogue

CoreAssassinSoulknifeThief & Scion

Sneak Attack choices, defensive reactions and subclass follow-ups stay connected to the attack, damage and save cards.

Sneak Attack, Cunning Strike and defense

  • Sneak Attack. Eligible finesse/ranged attacks recommend the rider when Advantage applies or a conscious ally is within 5 feet of the recorded target without effective Disadvantage. Manual selection remains available. Damage follows the weapon type, supports criticals and is tracked once per turn.
  • Cunning Strike. Choose Poison, Trip or Withdraw in damage configuration. Their Sneak Attack dice cost is deducted before critical scaling. Improved Cunning Strike permits two distinct choices with their combined cost. Poison prompts end-turn Constitution repeat saves; Trip applies Prone on failure. Withdraw movement remains manual.
  • Devious Strikes. Daze, Obscure and Knock Out use the owned native saves/effects. Daze and Obscure end at the end of the target’s next turn. Knock Out gets its repeat save and ends on damage. Daze’s action decisions stay at the table.
  • Uncanny Dodge. The owner/GM gets a button on a confirmed incoming attack’s damage card. Spend the Reaction and set only that Rogue’s damage multiplier to half, retaining native resistances and Undo. Seeing the attacker is confirmed by the click. Use before applying damage.
  • Evasion. Available to anyone owning the feature: qualifying Dexterity saves that normally deal half on success use zero on success and half on failure. Incapacitated creatures are excluded. Save summaries label Evasion holders; native resistance and immunity still apply.

Assassin

  • Assassinate. Recommend target-specific first-round Advantage against combatants that have not taken a turn. Surprising Strikes adds the native Rogue-level damage to qualifying first-round Sneak Attack hits without doubling that flat bonus on a critical.
  • Envenom Weapons. Failed initial and repeat Cunning Strike Poison saves prompt the native extra Poison damage. Ignore Poison resistance while preserving immunity. Successful repeat saves end Poison normally.
  • Death Strike. A first-round Sneak Attack hit offers the native Constitution save without duplicating Sneak Attack damage. HP application waits for the result; failure seeds double damage while retaining original dice and correction controls.

Soulknife

  • Homing Strikes. A missed Psychic Blade attack can add its native Psionic Energy Die without rerolling the original d20. Spend the die only if the miss becomes a hit, then resume the linked damage flow.
  • Rend Mind. A qualifying Psychic Blade Sneak Attack damage card offers Rend Mind. Prefer its free use, otherwise spend three Soulknife dice. Failure applies Stunned with end-turn repeat saves. The Fighter’s Energy Die pool stays separate.

Thief, Scion and manual subclasses

  • Thief’s Reflexes. Round one gets a second combat-tracker entry for the same token at Initiative minus 10. It mirrors the source entry and is removed after its turn, without creating a second creature.
  • Scion of the Three · Terrify. Strike Fear adds Terrify to Cunning Strike configuration. Deduct one Sneak Attack die, prompt the native Wisdom save and apply Frightened on failure with end-turn repeat saves. Its attack Advantage is specific to the originating Rogue.
  • Leave one-off choices manual. Phantom follow-up targeting, Arcane Trickster choices and the other deferred Scion features stay on their native cards.

Sorcerer

Pure magic, embodied. Control the battlefield, transmute your spells, and overpower your enemies with raw magical force. Let the system handle Metamagic choices during casting and carry them into damage, keeping those decisions connected to the spell instead of managing extra cards afterward.

  • Innate Sorcery While its effect is active, Sorcerer spell attacks recommend advantage. Other classes’ spells and weapon attacks are excluded; other advantage/disadvantage sources still combine normally.
  • Transmuted Spell Choose an eligible elemental damage type before rolling. The choice follows subsequent damage from that casting, with no repeated Sorcery Point charge.
  • Heightened Spell Choose one target before its save. Disadvantage combines with other sources, so Magic Resistance can cancel it to a normal save.
  • Careful Spell Select protected creatures before rolling. It records automatic successes and prevents half-on-save damage for those creatures. Protection does not remove targets from a nonselective spell.
  • Empowered Spell The spell damage card offers a feature-icon action. Select active damage dice up to the Charisma modifier, minimum one, then confirm to spend 1 Sorcery Point and keep the new results, even when lower. Opening the picker hands automatic application back to manual control; applied damage must first be undone.
  • Seeking Spell A missed spell attack offers a reroll action. Spend 1 Sorcery Point to reroll one d20 and use the new result; linked hit/critical results update, with a damage prompt on a hit.
  • Costs, combinations, and card tags Cast-time choices respect supported Sorcery Incarnate / active Innate Sorcery combination limits and Arcane Apotheosis free-use accounting. Empowered and Seeking remain result-card options. Tags show the applied Metamagic, with element and target details in tooltips.

Warlock

  • Eldritch Smite An eligible pact-weapon hit offers a default-No damage rider. Yes spends a Pact Magic slot, scales Force damage with that slot’s level, and marks the feature used for the combat turn. It does not consume a bonus action.

Hex, Conjure Minor Elementals, and the Eldritch Blast remaining-attacks window are described under Spells.
